title: Estar + Participle: What Potosí Looks Like Today

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *estar* + participle from B2 Unit 20. *Ser* + participle tells the action (*Potosí fue fundada en 1545*), and *estar* + participle tells the result you can see now (*La casa está convertida en museo*). The participle agrees with the subject, like an adjective. The history of Potosí gives you both: what happened, and what is left today.

sections.title: Action and result in Potosí
rows: La Casa de la Moneda está convertida en museo.
The Mint is turned into a museum. (the result, now)
El cerro está perforado por muchos túneles.
The hill is riddled with tunnels. (the result)
La ciudad está inscrita en la lista de la UNESCO desde 1987.
The city has been on the UNESCO list since 1987. (the result)

items.spanish: La ciudad está situada al pie del Cerro Rico.
items.english: The city is situated at the foot of the Cerro Rico.

items.spanish: La plata fue llevada a la Casa de la Moneda.
items.english: The silver was taken to the Mint. (the action)

sections.content: Ask yourself: am I telling what happened, or what I can see now? *Fue convertida* is an event; *está convertida* is the state. A time word such as *hoy*, *ahora* or *desde* points to *estar*.
